## Downloads

Materials for the spinviz workshop, covering the full workflow from loading
data to saving a body heatmap and a tissue/pathology sunburst:

- [Workshop slides (PDF)](../workshop/spinviz_workshop_slides.pdf)
- [R script](../workshop/spinviz_workshop.R): step-by-step script with
  activities and answers
- [body_injuries_example.csv](../workshop/body_injuries_example.csv): example
  data for `plot_heatmap()` (boxing and judo)
- [tissue_injuries_example.csv](../workshop/tissue_injuries_example.csv):
  example data for `plot_sunburst()` (boxing and judo)

To download a file, right-click the link and choose **Save link as...**.

## Setup

Install spinviz from GitHub, then load it:

```{r}
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("bnqcasimiro/spinviz")
library(spinviz)
```

Saving a sunburst as an image also needs the optional `chromote` and
`base64enc` packages, plus Google Chrome:

```{r}
install.packages(c("chromote", "base64enc"))
```

## Loading the example data

The example CSV files follow the same layout as the templates created by
`create_injury_template()`. You can either:

- Download a CSV and read it in with `read_injury_data()`, or
- Use the built-in copies, `body_df` and `tissue_df`, which hold the same data

```{r}
download.file(
  "https://bnqcasimiro.github.io/spinviz/workshop/body_injuries_example.csv",
  destfile = "body_injuries_example.csv"
)
body_data <- read_injury_data("body_injuries_example.csv")

download.file(
  "https://bnqcasimiro.github.io/spinviz/workshop/tissue_injuries_example.csv",
  destfile = "tissue_injuries_example.csv"
)
tissue_data <- read_sunburst_data("tissue_injuries_example.csv")

# Or skip the CSV files:
body_data <- body_df
tissue_data <- tissue_df
```
